title: Victor Girard's dream city and Harry Warner's ranch
lede: Woodland Hills began as Girard, a 1922 subdivision by a flamboyant promoter named Victor Girard Kleinberger, who built false storefronts and a mosque-style tower to lure buyers and planted thousands of trees. His company failed, the trees grew, and in 1941 the town renamed itself for them. To the north, a movie mogul's horse ranch later became Warner Center.
tl: Victor Girard Kleinberger buys 2,886 acres and lays out the town of Girard, about 6,000 lots.
Girard builds gates, a mosque-style tower and a row of false-front stores to impress buyers.
Thousands of trees are planted along the new streets.
Harry Warner of Warner Bros. assembles a horse ranch of about 1,100 acres north of Ventura Boulevard.
Residents rename the community Woodland Hills.
Pierce College opens as an agricultural school, with a working farm.
The Warner family donates 20 acres for Warner Center Park as the ranch is planned into Warner Center.
On September 6, Pierce College records 121 degrees, the hottest temperature ever measured in LA County.

fact: lots in the original town of Girard
p: Victor Girard Kleinberger was a salesman with big ideas. In 1922 he bought nearly 2,900 acres of rolling grassland in the southwest Valley and divided it into about 6,000 lots. To make the empty land look like a town, he built entry gates, a tower in a Middle Eastern style and a row of false storefronts along Ventura Boulevard, and he planted thousands of trees. The Depression sank his company. The trees survived.

ch.h: A town named for its trees
p: By 1941 the trees had grown into the canopy that still shades the older streets, and residents voted to rename the community Woodland Hills. North of Ventura Boulevard, Harry Warner raised thoroughbreds on a ranch of about 1,100 acres. In the 1960s it was planned into Warner Center, now the west Valley's business district, and the family gave 20 acres for a park.

fact: LA County's record high, at Pierce in 2020
p: Pierce College opened in 1947 as an agricultural school and still runs a working farm with animals and fields in the middle of the suburbs. Its weather station holds Los Angeles County's all-time heat record, 121 degrees on September 6, 2020.

dyk: What was Woodland Hills called first?
Girard, after its founder Victor Girard Kleinberger. It was renamed in 1941.
What was Warner Center before the offices?
Where was LA County's hottest temperature recorded?
At Pierce College in Woodland Hills, 121 degrees on September 6, 2020.
